category: Phrasal verbs on regular bases: T-Z

entries.meaning: To add something extra at the end, often something small or unwelcome. ---
examples: The hotel tacks on a resort fee nobody mentions at booking.
They tacked two more questions on at the end of the form.
A delivery charge had been tacked on without any warning.
entries.separable: separable — tack on a service fee or tack a service fee on; with a pronoun it must split: tack it on, never ✗ tack on it. The thing it is added to takes to: tacked on to the bill.
entries.forms: tack on · tacked on · tacked on

entries.meaning: To go somewhere with other people who did not really invite you. ---
examples: Do you mind if I tag along?
Her little brother tagged along to every practice.
He's been tagging along with the crew all summer.
entries.русский: увязываться, увязаться (за кем-л.); идти следом, пойти следом
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the people you follow come after with: tag along with us.
entries.forms: tag along · tagged along · tagged along

entries.meaning: To become gradually smaller or weaker until it nearly stops. ---
examples: Ticket sales tailed off right after the holidays.
Donations always tail off in February.
Applications have been tailing off since the fee went up.
entries.русский: убывать, убыть; идти на убыль; сходить на нет
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: sales tailed off. Nothing can sit between the two words.
entries.forms: tail off · tailed off · tailed off

entries.meaning: To say things to someone on a particular subject. ---
examples: Can we talk about this tomorrow?
They talked about moving to Denver for the better part of an hour.
Everyone at work is talking about the merger.
entries.separable: inseparable — talk about the budget, never ✗ talk the budget about. English needs the about: ✗ talk the problem, and the same trap in reverse with discuss, which takes no preposition: discuss the budget.
entries.forms: talk about · talked about · talked about

entries.meaning: To keep discussing a subject without ever addressing it directly. ---
examples: He talked around the question for twenty minutes.
They kept talking around the real problem.
We have talked around this long enough — say it plainly.
entries.русский: обходить тему, говорить вокруг да около
entries.separable: inseparable in this sense — talk around the issue, never ✗ talk the issue around
entries.forms: talk around · talked around · talked around

entries.meaning: To persuade someone to change their mind by talking to them. ---
examples: She was against it, but he talked her around.
Give me ten minutes and I'll talk him around.
They had talked the whole committee around by lunch.
entries.separable: separable — talk her around, and talk around the problem (different sense, inseparable)
entries.forms: talk around · talked around · talked around

entries.meaning: To speak to someone without listening to anything they say back. ---
examples: He talks at you for an hour and calls it a meeting.
The consultant talked at us for ninety minutes straight.
I'm tired of being talked at in these trainings.
entries.русский: говорить, не слушая собеседника; вещать; отчитывать
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows the particle: talk at me, never ✗ talk me at. Compare talk to, which is a two-way conversation.
entries.forms: talk at · talked at · talked at

entries.meaning: To answer someone in authority rudely. ---
examples: Don't talk back to your teacher.
He talked back once and lost his phone for a week.
She's been talking back to everybody since she turned thirteen.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the person comes after to: talk back to your mother.
entries.forms: talk back · talked back · talked back

entries.meaning: To calm someone or persuade them to give up a dangerous plan by talking to them. ---
examples: A negotiator talked the man down from the bridge.
Her sister can usually talk her down when she starts panicking.
He was talked down by a dispatcher who stayed on the line for an hour.
entries.separable: separable — talk down the gunman, talk the gunman down; with a pronoun it must split: talk her down, never ✗ talk down her.
entries.forms: talk down · talked down · talked down

entries.meaning: To persuade a seller to accept a lower price. ---
examples: I talked the dealer down to nine thousand.
You can usually talk down the asking price on a used bike.
She is very good at talking landlords down a hundred dollars a month.
entries.русский: сбивать, сбить (цену); уговаривать, уговорить снизить цену
entries.separable: separable — talk down the price, talk the price down, talk him down to four hundred; never ✗ talk down him.
entries.forms: talk down · talked down · talked down

entries.meaning: To speak to someone as though they were less intelligent than you. ---
examples: Don't talk down to me — I read the same report you did.
The specialist talked down to her for the whole visit.
Nobody learns much from a teacher who is always talking down to the class.
entries.separable: inseparable in this sense, and it needs to: talk down to the audience, never ✗ talk the audience down to.
entries.forms: talk down · talked down · talked down

entries.meaning: To speak to someone as if they were less intelligent than you. ---
examples: The doctor never talks down to patients.
She felt talked down to in every meeting.
Stop talking down to me — I read the report too.
entries.separable: inseparable — the person always follows the whole phrase: talks down to his staff, never ✗ talks his staff down to.
entries.forms: talk down to · talked down to · talked down to
entries.third person: talks down to · -ing form: talking down to

entries.meaning: To persuade someone to do something they were not planning to do. ---
examples: Don't let him talk you into another timeshare.
She talked her parents into letting her go.
I got talked into running the half marathon.
entries.separable: always split — the person goes in the middle: talk her into it, never ✗ talk into her. What follows into is a noun or an -ing form: talked me into buying it.
entries.forms: talk into · talked into · talked into

entries.meaning: To discuss a problem thoroughly until it is settled. ---
examples: They sat on the porch and talked the whole thing out.
It's better to talk it out than to trade angry texts.
We've been talking out the details all week.
entries.русский: обсуждать, обсудить до конца; выяснять, выяснить отношения; проговаривать, проговорить
entries.separable: separable — talk out the problem, talk the problem out; with a pronoun it must split, and talk it out is the commonest form of all.
entries.forms: talk out · talked out · talked out

entries.meaning: To persuade someone not to do something they were planning to do. ---
examples: His friends talked him out of quitting.
You can't talk her out of anything once she's decided.
I was talked out of selling the car, and I'm glad.
entries.separable: always split — the person goes in the middle: talk him out of it, never ✗ talk out of him. What follows out of is a noun or an -ing form.
entries.forms: talk out of · talked out of · talked out of
entries.third person: talks out of · -ing form: talking out of

entries.meaning: To discuss something carefully with someone before deciding. ---
examples: Let me talk it over with my wife and call you tomorrow.
We talked over the budget for two hours.
They're still talking over whether to move.
entries.separable: separable — talk over the offer or talk the offer over; with a pronoun it must split: talk it over, never ✗ talk over it.
entries.forms: talk over · talked over · talked over

entries.meaning: To go over something step by step with someone until it is clear. ---
examples: Can you talk me through the installation?
We talked through every objection before the vote.
She's talking the new hire through the checklist right now.
entries.русский: разбирать по шагам, разобрать по шагам; подробно объяснять, объяснить
entries.separable: separable — talk through the steps or talk the steps through; with a pronoun it must split: talk it through. It also takes a person plus a thing: talk me through the setup.
entries.forms: talk through · talked through · talked through

entries.meaning: To praise something publicly so that other people get interested in it. ---
examples: The coach keeps talking up his freshman quarterback.
They talked the neighborhood up until prices doubled.
The movie was talked up so much that it couldn't possibly deliver.
entries.separable: separable — talk up the new album or talk the new album up; with a pronoun it must split: talk it up.
entries.forms: talk up · talked up · talked up

entries.meaning: To add numbers or items together to get a total. ---
examples: Let's tally up what we each owe.
She tallied the receipts up at closing time.
Once the mail-in ballots were tallied up, the race had flipped.
entries.separable: separable — tally up the votes or tally the votes up; with a pronoun it must split: tally them up.
entries.forms: tally up · tallied up · tallied up

entries.meaning: To reduce or hold back something that is growing too strong, like fear or excitement. ---
examples: The mayor tried to tamp down the panic.
Management tamped the rumors down with a company-wide email.
Prices are finally being tamped down by higher rates.
entries.separable: separable — tamp down expectations or tamp expectations down; with a pronoun it must split: tamp them down.
entries.forms: tamp down · tamped down · tamped down

entries.meaning: To twist something into a knot, or to get caught up in a mess you cannot easily get out of. ---
examples: The headphones tangle up the second you put them in a pocket.
He tangled the fishing line up on the first cast.
She got tangled up in a lawsuit that lasted three years.
entries.separable: separable — tangle up the cords or tangle the cords up; with a pronoun it must split: tangle them up. Very often passive: get tangled up in something.
entries.forms: tangle up · tangled up · tangled up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the wind tangled up the flag), intransitive (the leash tangles up every walk)

entries.meaning: To start using a supply of money, energy, or interest that was already there. ---
examples: The ad taps into a real fear about money.
They tapped into savings to cover the roof.
He's tapping into a market nobody else noticed.
entries.русский: получать доступ, получить доступ (к); использовать, задействовать
entries.separable: inseparable — what you reach always follows the whole phrase: tap into the market, never ✗ tap the market into.
entries.forms: tap into · tapped into · tapped into

entries.meaning: To quit or give up because you have nothing left. ---
examples: I'm tapping out — somebody else can finish the shift.
He tapped out after two hours of moving furniture.
Half the volunteers had tapped out by noon.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: he tapped out in the third round. Informal.
entries.forms: tap out · tapped out · tapped out

entries.meaning: To close or bind something with tape. ---
examples: Tape up the boxes before the movers get here.
The trainer taped his ankle up at halftime.
Every window was taped up before the storm.
entries.separable: separable — tape up the box or tape the box up; with a pronoun it must split: tape it up.
entries.forms: tape up · taped up · taped up

entries.meaning: To become gradually smaller or weaker until it stops. ---
examples: Traffic tapers off after seven.
The applause tapered off and the room went quiet.
Her doctor is tapering off the steroids over three weeks.
entries.русский: постепенно уменьшаться, уменьшиться; сходить на нет, сойти на нет
entries.separable: usually no object at all: the rain tapered off. When it does take one, keep it together: taper off the medication, not ✗ taper the medication off.
entries.forms: taper off · tapered off · tapered off
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (sales tapered off), transitive (taper off the dose)

entries.meaning: To tell an adult that another child has done something wrong. ---
examples: Nobody likes a kid who tattles on everyone.
She tattled on her brother for eating the cookies.
He's been tattling on the whole class all week.
entries.separable: inseparable — the person always follows the whole phrase: tattled on his sister, never ✗ tattled his sister on. Mostly children's English.
entries.forms: tattle on · tattled on · tattled on

entries.meaning: To join with another person or group to work on something together. ---
examples: Let's team up for the group project.
The two schools teamed up to run the food drive.
They're teaming up with a startup in Austin.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the partner comes after with: team up with a local charity.
entries.forms: team up · teamed up · teamed up

entries.meaning: To make someone annoyed or angry. ---
examples: Little things like that tee him off.
The surprise fee teed off half the customers.
She was teed off about being left out of the email.
entries.русский: выводить из себя, вывести из себя; злить, разозлить
entries.separable: separable — the person goes in the middle with a pronoun: that teed me off; with a noun either order works: teed off the whole staff. Usually heard in the passive: he was teed off. Informal.
entries.forms: tee off · teed off · teed off

entries.meaning: To get something ready so that it can happen next. ---
examples: Her opening remarks tee up the whole debate.
We teed up three interviews for Thursday.
The vote has been teed up for early next month.
entries.separable: separable — tee up the next question or tee the next question up; with a pronoun it must split: tee it up.
entries.forms: tee up · teed up · teed up

entries.meaning: To try something in order to see whether it works. ---
examples: Let's test out the projector before everyone shows up.
He tested the theory out on his own students.
The feature is being tested out with a few hundred users.
entries.separable: separable — test out the new oven or test the new oven out; with a pronoun it must split: test it out, never ✗ test out it.
entries.forms: test out · tested out · tested out

entries.meaning: To stop being frozen, or to make something stop being frozen. ---
examples: Thaw out the shrimp in cold water, not on the counter.
The lake finally thawed out in April.
My hands are still thawing out from the walk.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — thaw out the chicken or thaw the chicken out; with a pronoun it must split: thaw it out. It is just as common with no object: the pipes thawed out.
entries.forms: thaw out · thawed out · thawed out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (thaw out the steaks), intransitive (the ground is thawing out)

entries.meaning: To become fewer or less dense, or to make something fewer or less dense. ---
examples: The crowd thins out once the headliner finishes.
His hair thinned out in his thirties.
We spent Saturday thinning out the tomato plants.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — thin out the seedlings or thin the seedlings out; with a pronoun it must split: thin them out. Usually there is no object: the crowd thinned out.
entries.forms: thin out · thinned out · thinned out
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (traffic thins out after nine), transitive (thin out the carrots)

entries.meaning: To turn the pages of something quickly without reading carefully. ---
examples: He thumbs through the catalog every time it comes.
She thumbed through the report on the way to the meeting.
I was thumbing through an old photo album and found this.
entries.separable: inseparable — what you look through always follows the whole phrase: thumb through a magazine, never ✗ thumb a magazine through.
entries.forms: thumb through · thumbed through · thumbed through

entries.meaning: To make someone angry or irritated. ---
examples: It really ticks me off when people don't signal.
His joke ticked off everyone at the table.
She's still ticked off about the parking ticket.
entries.separable: separable — with a pronoun it must split: that ticks me off, never ✗ ticks off me; with a noun either order works: ticked off the neighbors. Very often passive: I'm ticked off. Informal.
entries.forms: tick off · ticked off · ticked off

entries.meaning: To give someone enough of something to get through a difficult period. ---
examples: Take twenty dollars — it should tide you over until payday.
A snack tided the kids over until dinner.
The loan is just tiding them over through the slow season.
entries.русский: выручать, выручить; помогать продержаться, помочь продержаться
entries.separable: separable, and the person almost always goes in the middle: tide me over, this will tide you over until Friday, never ✗ tide over me.
entries.forms: tide over · tided over · tided over

entries.meaning: To make a place neat by putting things where they belong. ---
examples: Can you tidy up the living room?
She tidied the whole apartment up in an hour.
He's tidying up his notes before he hands them in.
entries.русский: прибирать, прибрать; наводить порядок, навести порядок
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — tidy up the kitchen or tidy the kitchen up; with a pronoun it must split: tidy it up. Often no object at all: let's tidy up before they get here.
entries.forms: tidy up · tidied up · tidied up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (tidy up the desk), intransitive (I tidied up after dinner)

entries.meaning: To fasten something so it cannot move, or to limit someone's freedom. ---
examples: Tie down everything in the truck bed.
A mortgage tied them down more than they expected.
He's never wanted to be tied down to one city.
entries.русский: связывать по рукам и ногам; ограничивать, ограничить; привязывать, привязать
entries.separable: separable — tie down the tarp or tie the tarp down; with a pronoun it must split: tie it down. Of people, usually passive: I don't want to be tied down.
entries.forms: tie down · tied down · tied down

entries.meaning: To connect or fit well with something else. ---
examples: How does this tie in with what we discussed?
The ad campaign tied in with the movie release.
She's tying the survey results in with last year's numbers.
entries.separable: usually no object — what it connects to comes after with: ties in with the main story. When it does take an object it splits: tie the ending in with the opening.
entries.forms: tie in · tied in · tied in
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (that ties in nicely), transitive (tie the lesson in with the reading)

entries.meaning: To fasten something with rope or string so it cannot move or come apart. ---
examples: Tie up the trash bag before the raccoons find it.
He tied the boat up at the dock.
The robbers had tied up the guard and taken the keys.
entries.separable: separable — tie up the newspapers or tie the newspapers up; with a pronoun it must split: tie it up, never ✗ tie up it.
entries.forms: tie up · tied up · tied up

entries.meaning: To keep someone or something busy or unavailable for a while. ---
examples: Sorry, I'm tied up in meetings all morning.
The accident tied up traffic for two hours.
Inventory ties up most of their cash.
entries.separable: separable — tie up the phone line, tie the line up, tie it up. In this meaning it is mostly passive with people: I'm tied up until three.
entries.forms: tie up · tied up · tied up

entries.meaning: To make something stricter, tighter, or better organized. ---
examples: We need to tighten up the hiring process.
The airline tightened its refund policy up last year.
Security has been tightened up since the break-in.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — tighten up security or tighten security up; with a pronoun it must split: tighten it up. Also used with no object: the defense tightened up.
entries.forms: tighten up · tightened up · tightened up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (tighten up the rules), intransitive (his shoulders tightened up)

entries.meaning: To secretly warn someone about something, especially something illegal or about to happen. ---
examples: One careless question can tip off the seller.
A neighbor tipped the police off about the noise.
The suspects had clearly been tipped off.
entries.русский: предупреждать, предупредить (тайно); давать наводку, дать наводку
entries.separable: separable — tip off the police or tip the police off; with a pronoun it must split: tip them off, never ✗ tip off them.
entries.forms: tip off · tipped off · tipped off

entries.meaning: To fall onto its side, or to push something onto its side. ---
examples: That bookshelf will tip over if you don't anchor it.
She tipped the wheelbarrow over by accident.
Two chairs had been tipped over in the scuffle.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — tip over the bucket or tip the bucket over; with a pronoun it must split: tip it over. Just as often there is no object: the lamp tipped over.
entries.forms: tip over · tipped over · tipped over
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the dog tipped over his water bowl), intransitive (the canoe tipped over)

entries.meaning: To make someone completely exhausted. ---
examples: A long walk tires out the puppy for the whole evening.
The hike tired us out more than we expected.
She was tired out before the day even started.
entries.separable: separable — tire out the kids or tire the kids out; with a pronoun it must split: tire them out, never ✗ tire out them.
entries.forms: tire out · tired out · tired out

entries.meaning: To make something less strong, less extreme, or less loud. ---
examples: Tone it down — the baby is asleep.
The studio toned down the ending after test screenings.
His speech had been toned down by the lawyers.
entries.separable: separable — tone down the language or tone the language down; with a pronoun it must split: tone it down, never ✗ tone down it.
entries.forms: tone down · toned down · toned down

entries.meaning: To make muscles firmer and stronger through exercise. ---
examples: Swimming tones up your whole back.
He toned his core up over one winter.
She's been toning up since January.
entries.русский: подтягивать, подтянуть (мышцы); приводить в форму, привести в форму
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — tone up your arms or tone your arms up; with a pronoun it must split: tone them up. Also used with no object: I'm trying to tone up.
entries.forms: tone up · toned up · toned up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (tone up your legs), intransitive (she's toning up for the wedding)

entries.meaning: To fill something the rest of the way to the top. ---
examples: Can I top off your coffee?
He topped the tank off before the road trip.
The pool gets topped off every couple of weeks in summer.
entries.separable: separable — top off the tank or top the tank off; with a pronoun it must split: top it off, never ✗ top off it.
entries.forms: top off · topped off · topped off

entries.meaning: To finish something in a memorable way, usually with one last thing. ---
examples: They topped off the weekend with a barbecue.
A pay raise topped the year off nicely.
And to top it off, my flight was canceled.
entries.separable: separable — top off the meal with dessert, top the evening off; with a pronoun it must split, and the fixed phrase to top it off means "and on top of everything else".
entries.forms: top off · topped off · topped off

entries.meaning: To reach the highest level and go no higher. ---
examples: The trail tops out at nine thousand feet.
Sales topped out in 2019 and slid after that.
Temperatures are topping out in the low nineties this week.
entries.русский: достигать максимума, достичь максимума; выходить на предел, выйти на предел
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the number comes after at: topped out at 95 degrees.
entries.forms: top out · topped out · topped out

entries.meaning: To discuss ideas or suggestions informally, without deciding yet. ---
examples: We're tossing around a few names for the store.
They tossed the idea around over lunch.
That number has been tossed around for months with no proof.
entries.separable: separable — toss around a few ideas or toss a few ideas around; with a pronoun it must split: toss them around.
entries.forms: toss around · tossed around · tossed around

entries.meaning: To reject or dismiss something officially. ---
examples: The judge could toss out the whole lawsuit.
An appeals court tossed the conviction out.
Their proposal was tossed out in the first round.
entries.separable: separable — toss out the case or toss the case out; with a pronoun it must split: toss it out. Common in news about courts.
entries.forms: toss out · tossed out · tossed out

entries.meaning: To throw something away because you no longer want it. ---
examples: Just toss out anything that's expired.
He tossed the whole box out without looking inside.
Two bags of clothes were tossed out in the cleanup.
entries.separable: separable — toss out the leftovers or toss the leftovers out; with a pronoun it must split: toss it out, never ✗ toss out it.
entries.forms: toss out · tossed out · tossed out

entries.meaning: To make brief contact with someone to share news or check on something. ---
examples: Let's touch base on Monday.
I touched base with the vendor this morning.
She's touching base with everyone before the launch.
entries.русский: связываться, связаться; выходить на связь, выйти на связь
entries.separable: fixed — the object is always base and nothing else goes there: touch base with the client, never ✗ touch the base. The person comes after with. Common in American work English.
entries.forms: touch base · touched base · touched base
entries.transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object base

entries.meaning: To land, said of an aircraft or of a tornado reaching the ground. ---
examples: We touch down in Denver at 4:15.
The flight touched down twenty minutes early.
A tornado had touched down just west of town.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: the plane touched down at six.
entries.forms: touch down · touched down · touched down

entries.meaning: To cause something big and sudden to start, like a fight or a panic. ---
examples: One rumor can touch off a run on the bank.
The verdict touched off protests in three cities.
A single spark touched off the fire that burned the block.
entries.separable: separable, though the object is usually long and stays at the end: touched off a wave of protests; with a pronoun it splits: touched it off.
entries.forms: touch off · touched off · touched off

entries.meaning: To improve something with small corrections or additions. ---
examples: I need to touch up the trim around the door.
She touched her makeup up before the photos.
Every picture in the catalog has been touched up.
entries.separable: separable — touch up the paint or touch the paint up; with a pronoun it must split: touch it up, never ✗ touch up it.
entries.forms: touch up · touched up · touched up

entries.meaning: To keep going through something painful or difficult instead of giving up. ---
examples: No painkillers — he just toughs it out.
They toughed it out through two years of construction.
She's toughing it out until the contract ends.
entries.русский: терпеть, вытерпеть; выдерживать, выдержать; держаться до конца
entries.separable: fixed — the object is always it: tough it out, never ✗ tough the winter out. Informal.
entries.forms: tough it out · toughed it out · toughed it out
entries.third person: toughs it out · -ing form: toughing it out
entries.transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object it

entries.meaning: To become stronger and better able to handle hardship, or to make someone or something stronger. ---
examples: You toughen up quickly on a job like that.
Two winters in Chicago toughened him up.
The state is toughening up its emissions rules.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — toughen up the rules or toughen the rules up; with a pronoun it must split: toughen him up. Often no object: you'll toughen up.
entries.forms: toughen up · toughened up · toughened up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (he toughened up fast), transitive (boot camp toughened them up)

entries.meaning: To pull a vehicle away with a truck, usually because it is parked illegally or broken down. ---
examples: They tow away anything left overnight in that lot.
The city towed my van away on street-cleaning day.
Three cars were being towed away when I walked by.
entries.русский: эвакуировать (машину); увозить на эвакуаторе, увезти на эвакуаторе
entries.separable: separable — tow away the car or tow the car away; with a pronoun it must split: tow it away. Usually passive: my car got towed away.
entries.forms: tow away · towed away · towed away

entries.meaning: To find someone or something after searching hard. ---
examples: It took a week to track down the right part.
She tracked her birth mother down through a DNA site.
Police are still tracking down witnesses.
entries.separable: separable — track down the owner or track the owner down; with a pronoun it must split: track him down, never ✗ track down him.
entries.forms: track down · tracked down · tracked down

entries.meaning: To give something old to a seller as part of the payment for something new. ---
examples: You can trade in the old console for store credit.
They traded the minivan in for a pickup.
My laptop was traded in for about two hundred dollars.
entries.русский: сдавать в зачёт, сдать в зачёт (старое при покупке нового)
entries.separable: separable — trade in your old phone or trade your old phone in; with a pronoun it must split: trade it in. What you get instead comes after for.
entries.forms: trade in · traded in · traded in

entries.meaning: To use something, often unfairly, to get an advantage for yourself. ---
examples: He trades on his father's name every chance he gets.
The company traded on its reputation long after the quality slipped.
She got the job without trading on anyone's connections.
entries.русский: пользоваться, воспользоваться (в своих интересах); спекулировать (на чём-л.)
entries.separable: inseparable — trade on his reputation, never ✗ trade his reputation on.
entries.forms: trade on · traded on · traded on

entries.meaning: To replace what you have with a better or more expensive version. ---
examples: A lot of buyers trade up after the first kid.
They traded up to a three-bedroom last spring.
She's trading up to a better camera this year.
entries.русский: менять на лучшее, поменять на лучшее; переходить на более дорогое
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; what you move to comes after to: trade up to a bigger house.
entries.forms: trade up · traded up · traded up

entries.meaning: To get quieter and quieter until it stops, especially a voice. ---
examples: He starts a story and then just trails off.
Her voice trailed off when she saw who was listening.
The applause was trailing off by the time she reached the stage.
entries.русский: затихать, затихнуть; смолкать, смолкнуть; сходить на нет
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: her voice trailed off.
entries.forms: trail off · trailed off · trailed off

entries.meaning: To fit something out with a lot of showy extras. ---
examples: He tricked out his pickup with light bars and chrome.
They trick these vans out for weekend camping.
The studio came tricked out with gear he never once used.
entries.separable: separable — trick out the truck, trick the truck out, trick it out; never ✗ trick out it. The participle is very common as an adjective: a tricked-out van.
entries.forms: trick out · tricked out · tricked out

entries.meaning: To arrive slowly, a few at a time, instead of all at once. ---
examples: People trickle in for about an hour after the doors open.
Results trickled in all night.
Donations are still trickling in from the mailing.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: the guests trickled in.
entries.forms: trickle in · trickled in · trickled in

entries.meaning: To make a mistake, or to cause someone to make one. ---
examples: Irregular verbs trip up almost everybody.
The lawyer tripped the witness up on a date.
He's tripping up over the same two sounds every time.
entries.русский: сбивать с толку, сбить с толку; ошибаться, ошибиться; подставлять подножку
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — the question tripped her up, tripped up a lot of students; with a pronoun it must split: trip you up. Also used with no object: he tripped up on the last line.
entries.forms: trip up · tripped up · tripped up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (that detail trips people up), intransitive (she tripped up once)

entries.meaning: To bring up the same old argument, story, or excuse again. ---
examples: Every election they trot out the same slogans.
He trotted that story out at dinner again.
The statistic keeps being trotted out without context.
entries.русский: вытаскивать на свет, вытащить на свет; приводить одни и те же доводы
entries.separable: separable — trot out the same excuse or trot the same excuse out; with a pronoun it must split: trot it out. Usually disapproving.
entries.forms: trot out · trotted out · trotted out

entries.meaning: To invent a false accusation against someone. ---
examples: They trumped up a theft charge to keep him in jail.
The journalist was arrested on trumped-up charges.
Investigators found the department had been trumping up violations for years.
entries.separable: separable in principle — trump up charges, trump them up — but it is almost always heard in the passive or before a noun: trumped-up charges.
entries.forms: trump up · trumped up · trumped up

entries.meaning: To put on a piece of clothing to see whether it fits and looks right. ---
examples: Try on the other size before you decide.
She tried four dresses on and bought none of them.
He's trying on boots in the back.
entries.separable: separable — try on the jacket or try the jacket on; with a pronoun it must split: try it on, never ✗ try on it.
entries.forms: try on · tried on · tried on

entries.meaning: To use something for the first time to see how good it is. ---
examples: Let's try out that taco place on Fifth.
I tried the trial version out for a week.
The recipe is being tried out on the family first.
entries.separable: separable — try out the new app or try the new app out; with a pronoun it must split: try it out, never ✗ try out it.
entries.forms: try out · tried out · tried out

entries.meaning: To compete or audition for a place on a team or in a performance. ---
examples: She's going to try out for varsity in the fall.
He tried out for the school play and got the lead.
Forty kids are trying out for twelve spots.
entries.русский: проходить отбор, пройти отбор; пробоваться (в команду)
entries.separable: inseparable — nothing goes inside: try out for the team, never ✗ try the team out for. American schools use this for sports and plays alike.
entries.forms: try out for · tried out for · tried out for
entries.third person: tries out for · -ing form: trying out for

entries.meaning: To put something in a safe, hidden, or out-of-the-way place. ---
examples: She tucks away a little from every paycheck.
He tucked the letter away in a drawer.
The cabin is tucked away at the end of a dirt road.
entries.русский: убирать, убрать (подальше); прятать, спрятать; откладывать, отложить
entries.separable: separable — tuck away some money or tuck the money away; with a pronoun it must split: tuck it away. Of places it is usually passive: a café tucked away on a side street.
entries.forms: tuck away · tucked away · tucked away

entries.meaning: To push the bottom of a shirt inside your pants or skirt. ---
examples: Tuck in your shirt before the interview.
He tucked his shirt in and straightened his tie.
Her blouse was tucked in on one side only.
entries.separable: separable — tuck in your shirt or tuck your shirt in; with a pronoun it must split: tuck it in.
entries.forms: tuck in · tucked in · tucked in

entries.meaning: To put a child to bed and pull the covers snugly around them. ---
examples: Dad tucks them in every night.
She tucked in the twins and read one story.
He likes being tucked in even though he's nine.
entries.русский: укладывать спать, уложить спать; укрывать, укрыть (одеялом)
entries.separable: separable — tuck in the kids or tuck the kids in; with a pronoun it must split: tuck them in, never ✗ tuck in them.
entries.forms: tuck in · tucked in · tucked in

entries.meaning: To turn on a radio or television program in order to watch or listen. ---
examples: Tune in tomorrow at eight for the finale.
Nine million people tuned in to the debate.
Fans have been tuning in every Sunday since September.
entries.русский: настраиваться, настроиться (на волну); смотреть, посмотреть; слушать передачу
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object; the channel or show comes after to: tune in to channel 7.
entries.forms: tune in · tuned in · tuned in

entries.meaning: To stop paying attention to someone or something. ---
examples: Students tune out about forty minutes in.
She tuned the argument out and kept reading.
He's been tuning out the news for his own sanity.
entries.русский: отключаться, отключиться; переставать слушать, перестать слушать
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — tune out the noise or tune the noise out; with a pronoun it must split: tune it out. Just as common with no object: he tuned out halfway through.
entries.forms: tune out · tuned out · tuned out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (tune out the noise), intransitive (I tuned out after ten minutes)

entries.meaning: To adjust an engine or an instrument so that it runs or sounds right. ---
examples: Get the truck tuned up before winter.
He tuned the piano up the morning of the recital.
The orchestra was still tuning up when we sat down.
entries.separable: separable — tune up the engine or tune the engine up; with a pronoun it must split: tune it up. Musicians also use it with no object: the orchestra is tuning up.
entries.forms: tune up · tuned up · tuned up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (tune up the car), intransitive (the band tuned up backstage)

entries.meaning: To stop supporting someone and start opposing them, or to make someone do that. ---
examples: Public opinion turns against a mayor fast in a scandal.
His own party turned against him after the vote.
She accused him of turning the children against her.
entries.русский: ополчаться, ополчиться (на); восстанавливать против, восстановить против
entries.separable: inseparable when there is no other object — the crowd turned against him. In the transitive pattern the person influenced comes first: turned the kids against their father.
entries.forms: turn against · turned against · turned against
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (voters turned against the plan), transitive (he turned them against her)

entries.meaning: To change something failing into something successful. ---
examples: A new coach could turn around this season.
She turned the failing store around in two years.
The business has been turned around completely.
entries.separable: separable — turn around the company or turn the company around; with a pronoun it must split: turn it around.
entries.forms: turn around · turned around · turned around

entries.meaning: To face the other way, or to make something face or go the other way. ---
examples: Turn around — you've got something on your back.
She turned the car around at the state line.
He kept turning around to see who was following.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — turn the car around, turn it around. Just as common with no object: turn around and look.
entries.forms: turn around · turned around · turned around
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (he turned around), transitive (turn the truck around)

entries.meaning: To refuse to let someone in or to help them. ---
examples: The shelter never turns away anyone in winter.
They turned us away because we had no reservation.
Dozens of families were turned away at the border.
entries.русский: не пускать, не пустить; отказывать, отказать (во входе)
entries.separable: separable — turn away customers or turn customers away; with a pronoun it must split: turn them away. Often passive: we were turned away at the door.
entries.forms: turn away · turned away · turned away

entries.meaning: To go back the way you came, or to make someone go back. ---
examples: If the road is flooded, turn back.
We turned back two miles from the summit.
Rangers were turning hikers back all afternoon.
entries.русский: поворачивать назад, повернуть назад; возвращаться, вернуться
entries.separable: usually no object — we turned back at the pass. With an object it splits: turn the hikers back.
entries.forms: turn back · turned back · turned back
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (they turned back), transitive (the storm turned the climbers back)

entries.meaning: To reduce the volume, heat, or brightness of something. ---
examples: Turn down the TV — I'm on the phone.
He turned the heat down to sixty-eight.
The lights were turned down for the slideshow.
entries.русский: убавлять, убавить; делать тише, сделать тише
entries.separable: separable — turn down the music or turn the music down; with a pronoun it must split: turn it down.
entries.forms: turn down · turned down · turned down

entries.meaning: To refuse an offer, a request, or a person. ---
examples: You don't turn down a job like that.
They turned her down for the loan twice.
His application was turned down without explanation.
entries.separable: separable — turn down the offer or turn the offer down; with a pronoun it must split: turn it down, never ✗ turn down it.
entries.forms: turn down · turned down · turned down

entries.meaning: To go to bed. ---
examples: I think I'll turn in early tonight.
They turned in right after the news.
He was turning in around nine all week.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: I'm going to turn in. Slightly old-fashioned but still common.
entries.forms: turn in · turned in · turned in

entries.meaning: To hand someone over to the police, including yourself. ---
examples: Reward money makes people turn in their own neighbors.
The suspect turned himself in Tuesday morning.
She was turned in by an anonymous caller.
entries.русский: сдавать полиции, сдать полиции; выдавать, выдать
entries.separable: separable — with a pronoun it must split: turn him in, never ✗ turn in him; with a noun either order works. Reflexive use is common: she turned herself in.
entries.forms: turn in · turned in · turned in

entries.meaning: To hand something to a teacher, a boss, or an office. ---
examples: Turn in the permission slip by Friday.
She turned her resignation in on Monday.
Only nine essays have been turned in.
entries.separable: separable — turn in your homework or turn your homework in; with a pronoun it must split: turn it in, never ✗ turn in it.
entries.forms: turn in · turned in · turned in

entries.meaning: To become something different, or to change something into something different. ---
examples: A small disagreement can turn into a real fight.
They turned the old mill into apartments.
The drizzle was turning into sleet by dinnertime.
entries.separable: inseparable when there is no other object — turned into a nightmare. In the transitive pattern the thing changed comes first: turned the garage into an office.
entries.forms: turn into · turned into · turned into
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (it turned into a fight), transitive (they turned the attic into a bedroom)

entries.meaning: To make someone lose interest or feel disgusted. ---
examples: The smell of the place turns most people off immediately.
His tone turned off everyone in the room.
A lot of customers were turned off by the new pricing.
entries.русский: отталкивать, оттолкнуть; вызывать отвращение, вызвать отвращение
entries.separable: separable — with a pronoun it must split: it turns me off, never ✗ turns off me; with a noun either order works: turned off a lot of voters.
entries.forms: turn off · turned off · turned off

entries.meaning: To stop a machine, light, or supply from running. ---
examples: Turn off the oven when the timer goes.
She turned the water off at the main.
Notifications have been turned off since Friday.
entries.separable: separable — turn off the light or turn the light off; with a pronoun it must split: turn it off, never ✗ turn off it.
entries.forms: turn off · turned off · turned off

entries.meaning: To come to an event in a crowd. ---
examples: Hundreds turn out for the parade every year.
Only forty people turned out in the rain.
Voters have been turning out early all week.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: thousands turned out. The related noun is turnout.
entries.forms: turn out · turned out · turned out

entries.meaning: To prove in the end to be a certain way. ---
examples: It turns out she'd been right the whole time.
The rumor turned out to be false.
Everything is turning out better than we expected.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — it is followed by to be, by an adjective, or by a that clause: it turned out that he was right.
entries.forms: turn out · turned out · turned out

entries.meaning: To switch off a light. ---
examples: Turn out the lights when you leave.
He turned the lamp out and lay there thinking.
Every light in the house had been turned out.
entries.separable: separable — turn out the lights or turn the lights out; with a pronoun it must split: turn them out. Used mainly of lights; for machines say turn off.
entries.forms: turn out · turned out · turned out

entries.meaning: To give something or someone to an authority that has the right to it. ---
examples: The company must turn over the emails by Friday.
They turned the suspect over to federal agents.
All the evidence has been turned over to the court.
entries.separable: separable — turn over the documents or turn the documents over; with a pronoun it must split: turn them over. The receiver comes after to: turned it over to the FBI.
entries.forms: turn over · turned over · turned over

entries.meaning: To move something so the other side is up, or to roll onto your other side. ---
examples: Turn over the card and read the answer.
He turned the burgers over too early.
She turned over and pulled the blanket up.
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — turn over the pancakes or turn the pancakes over; with a pronoun it must split: turn it over. Also with no object: turn over and go back to sleep.
entries.forms: turn over · turned over · turned over
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (turn the mattress over), intransitive (he turned over in bed)

entries.meaning: To arrive or appear somewhere, often unexpectedly. ---
examples: Half the guests turn up after eight.
He turned up at my door with no warning.
She's been turning up late all month.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object: he turned up an hour late.
entries.forms: turn up · turned up · turned up

entries.meaning: To be found by chance after being lost. ---
examples: Lost phones usually turn up in the lost and found.
The ring turned up in the couch cushions.
Nothing has turned up in the search so far.
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the lost thing is the subject: my keys turned up.
entries.forms: turn up · turned up · turned up

entries.meaning: To increase the volume, heat, or intensity of something. ---
examples: Turn up the radio — this is my song.
She turned the thermostat up two degrees.
The pressure is being turned up on the mayor.
entries.русский: прибавлять, прибавить; делать громче, сделать громче
entries.separable: separable — turn up the volume or turn the volume up; with a pronoun it must split: turn it up, never ✗ turn up it.
entries.forms: turn up · turned up · turned up

entries.meaning: To enter information using a keyboard. ---
examples: Type in the code they texted you.
He typed the address in wrong twice.
Your password is never stored after it's typed in.
entries.separable: separable — type in the code or type the code in; with a pronoun it must split: type it in.
entries.forms: type in · typed in · typed in

entries.meaning: To turn handwritten or spoken material into a typed document. ---
examples: Can you type up the minutes from Tuesday?
She typed her notes up the same evening.
The interview is being typed up right now.
entries.separable: separable — type up the notes or type the notes up; with a pronoun it must split: type them up, never ✗ type up them.
entries.forms: type up · typed up · typed up

entries.meaning: To get rid of something you don't want by passing or selling it to someone else. ---
examples: He unloaded his old minivan on his nephew.
They're trying to unload the unsold units on small investors.
She's unloading her old textbooks on anyone who'll take them.
entries.separable: the thing you are getting rid of goes straight after the verb and the person after on: unload the old van on his nephew, unload it on me; ✗ unload on his nephew the old van
entries.forms: unload on · unloaded on · unloaded on

entries.meaning: To let out all your anger at someone in a rush of criticism. ---
examples: The coach unloaded on the referee after the call.
Don't unload on the intern — it wasn't her decision.
He's been unloading on everyone in the office all week.
entries.separable: inseparable — the person on the receiving end follows on: unload on the refs, unload on him, never ✗ unload him on
entries.forms: unload on · unloaded on · unloaded on

entries.meaning: To encourage someone to keep going or to try harder. ---
examples: The crowd urged her on down the final stretch.
His coach has urged him on since he was nine.
Parents lined the course, urging on the smallest runners.
entries.separable: separable, and it normally splits — the person or animal sits in the middle: the crowd urged her on; urge on the runners is possible but bookish, and a pronoun can never follow: ✗ urged on her
entries.forms: urge on · urged on · urged on

entries.meaning: To consume all of something so that none of it is left. ---
examples: Don't use up all the hot water — I still need a shower.
The kids used the last of the printer paper up on Monday.
We're using up the leftovers before the trip.
entries.separable: separable — use up the last of the milk, use the last of the milk up; a pronoun must sit in the middle: use it up, never ✗ use up it
entries.forms: use up · used up · used up

entries.meaning: To mark or bring about the beginning of a new period. ---
examples: One ruling like that can usher in years of litigation.
The 2008 crash ushered in a decade of caution.
Cheap sensors are ushering in a new kind of farming.
entries.separable: separable — usher in a new era, usher a new era in; in practice it rarely splits, but a pronoun goes in the middle: usher it in, never ✗ usher in it
entries.forms: usher in · ushered in · ushered in

entries.meaning: To mark the end of a period, or to move something aside as it ends. ---
examples: The ceremony ushers out the old year at midnight.
That election ushered out forty years of one-party rule.
The company is quietly ushering out its paper forms.
entries.separable: separable — usher out the old system, usher the old system out, usher it out; never ✗ usher out it
entries.forms: usher out · ushered out · ushered out

entries.meaning: To drift away from the subject or the plan you were following. ---
examples: Every meeting veers off into office gossip.
He veered off topic about ten minutes in.
The project had veered badly off course by March.
entries.русский: отклоняться, отклониться (от темы); уходить, уйти в сторону
entries.separable: no object — the meeting veered off again; a topic follows off directly: veered off topic, veered off course
entries.forms: veer off · veered off · veered off

entries.meaning: To turn suddenly to one side, leaving the course you were on. ---
examples: The truck veered off and clipped a guardrail.
A car had veered off the road in the ice.
Watch the front wheel — it keeps veering off to the left.
entries.separable: no object of its own — the truck veered off; when a road follows, off takes it and nothing can come between: veered off the highway, never ✗ veered the highway off
entries.forms: veer off · veered off · veered off

entries.meaning: To do nothing at all for a while, usually in front of a screen. ---
examples: I just want to veg out in front of the TV tonight.
We vegged out all Sunday and regretted nothing.
He's been vegging out since finals ended.
entries.русский: бездельничать, побездельничать; отдыхать, отдохнуть (ничего не делая)
entries.separable: no object — veg out on the couch; nothing can come between the two words
entries.forms: veg out · vegged out · vegged out

entries.meaning: To start doing something new and risky, especially a new line of business. ---
examples: The studio ventured into video games and lost a fortune.
Few small banks venture into crypto lending.
He's venturing into real estate at sixty.
entries.русский: браться, взяться (за новое дело); пробовать себя, попробовать себя (в новой области)
entries.separable: inseparable — the new field follows into: venture into politics, venture into it, never ✗ venture it into
entries.forms: venture into · ventured into · ventured into

entries.meaning: To go outside or leave a safe place when doing so takes some nerve. ---
examples: Nobody ventured out during the blizzard.
She rarely ventures out after dark.
We're venturing out for groceries once the rain stops.
entries.русский: выбираться, выбраться (наружу); отваживаться выйти, отважиться выйти
entries.separable: no object — nothing goes between the two words: venture out into the storm, never ✗ venture the storm out
entries.forms: venture out · ventured out · ventured out

entries.meaning: To spend a while sitting and talking with someone. ---
examples: We visited with the neighbors on the porch for an hour.
Come sit down and visit with us a while.
She's in the kitchen, visiting with my mother.
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows with: visit with your aunt, visit with her, never ✗ visit her with
entries.forms: visit with · visited with · visited with

entries.meaning: To reject a proposal by voting against it. ---
examples: The council voted down the parking plan 7–2.
The measure has been voted down twice already.
If they vote it down again, the project dies.
entries.separable: separable — vote down the amendment, vote the amendment down, vote it down; never ✗ vote down it
entries.forms: vote down · voted down · voted down

entries.meaning: To elect someone to a position by voting for them. ---
examples: They voted her in by a twenty-point margin.
If he won't budge, we'll vote in somebody who will.
The board has voted in a new chair.
entries.русский: избирать, избрать (на должность); проводить, провести (на выборах)
entries.separable: separable — vote in a new mayor, vote the new mayor in; a pronoun must split it: vote them in, never ✗ vote in them
entries.forms: vote in · voted in · voted in

entries.meaning: To force someone out of a contest or a show by voting against them. ---
examples: They vote one contestant off every Thursday.
The audience voted him off in week three.
She's terrified of being voted off before the finale.
entries.separable: separable — vote off the loudest player, vote him off; a pronoun has to split it: voted her off, never ✗ voted off her. Very often passive: he got voted off
entries.forms: vote off · voted off · voted off

entries.meaning: To settle a question by holding a vote about it. ---
examples: The board votes on the merger Thursday.
We voted on three different logos before anyone agreed.
They're still voting on whether to reopen the pool.
entries.русский: голосовать, проголосовать (по вопросу); ставить, поставить на голосование
entries.separable: inseparable — the question being decided follows on: vote on the proposal, vote on it, never ✗ vote it on
entries.forms: vote on · voted on · voted on

entries.meaning: To remove someone from office by voting against them at an election. ---
examples: Voters voted the mayor out after a single term.
Two senators were voted out last November.
They're threatening to vote the whole council out.
entries.русский: смещать, сместить (голосованием); не переизбирать, не переизбрать
entries.separable: separable — vote out the incumbent, vote the incumbent out, vote him out; never ✗ vote out him
entries.forms: vote out · voted out · voted out

entries.meaning: To approve something officially by voting for it. ---
examples: The committee voted through a watered-down version of the bill.
If they vote it through tonight, it takes effect in January.
The raise was voted through without a word of debate.
entries.separable: separable — vote through the budget, vote the budget through, vote it through; never ✗ vote through it
entries.forms: vote through · voted through · voted through

entries.meaning: To stay somewhere doing nothing while you wait for something to happen. ---
examples: I'm not going to wait around all day for the plumber.
We waited around for an hour and then left.
She's tired of waiting around for an answer.
entries.русский: ждать без дела, прождать; торчать в ожидании
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; what you are waiting for follows for: wait around for a callback.
entries.forms: wait around · waited around · waited around

entries.meaning: To serve food and drinks to customers, or to look after someone's every need. ---
examples: The same server waits on us every Sunday.
She waited on tables for six years to pay for school.
He has been waiting on the corner booth all night.
entries.separable: inseparable — wait on customers, wait on tables, never ✗ wait customers on.
entries.forms: wait on · waited on · waited on

entries.meaning: To wait for something or someone to arrive or to happen. ---
examples: We're still waiting on the lab results.
I waited on him for forty minutes outside the theater.
Half the office waits on one slow printer.
entries.separable: inseparable — wait on the results, never ✗ wait the results on. In American English this is interchangeable with wait for when you are waiting for something to arrive or happen.
entries.forms: wait on · waited on · waited on

entries.meaning: To stay where you are until something unpleasant is over. ---
examples: We waited out the rain under a gas station awning.
Sometimes there is nothing to do but wait it out.
They're waiting out the worst of the heat indoors.
entries.separable: separable — wait out the storm, wait the storm out, and a pronoun must split it: wait it out, never ✗ wait out it.
entries.forms: wait out · waited out · waited out

The whole team works around his schedule.
They're working around a broken oven all weekend.
entries.separable: inseparable — work around the problem, never ✗ work the problem around. The noun is one word: a workaround.
entries.forms: work around · worked around · worked around

entries.meaning: To fit something or someone into a schedule or a text that is already full. ---
examples: The dentist can work you in at four.
He worked in two jokes about the budget.
She's working a nap in before the red-eye.
entries.русский: втискивать, втиснуть (в расписание); включать, включить (между делом)
entries.separable: separable — work in a few jokes, work them in — and with a person it splits: can you work me in at three?
entries.forms: work in · worked in · worked in

entries.meaning: To get rid of a debt, extra weight, or a bad mood by working or exercising. ---
examples: He worked off the loan in two years.
She goes running to work off stress.
They're out in the yard working dinner off.
entries.separable: separable — work off the debt, work the calories off, work it off.
entries.forms: work off · worked off · worked off

entries.meaning: To keep trying to persuade someone to change their mind. ---
examples: He doesn't want to come, but I'm working on him.
The lobbyists worked on two senators for a month.
She has worked on her parents since the day the brochure arrived.
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows the particle: work on him, never ✗ work him on.
entries.forms: work on · worked on · worked on

entries.meaning: To spend time repairing something or making it better. ---
examples: I need to work on my Spanish before the trip.
He worked on that engine every weekend all winter.
She's been working on the same chapter since March.
entries.separable: inseparable — work on the car, never ✗ work the car on.
entries.forms: work on · worked on · worked on

entries.meaning: To end well, or to happen in a particular way in the end. ---
examples: Don't worry — this kind of thing usually works out.
The move worked out better than anyone expected.
Things have worked out fine for both of them.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: it all worked out. An adverb often follows: worked out great.
entries.forms: work out · worked out · worked out

entries.meaning: To exercise in order to get stronger or fitter. ---
examples: She works out before work every morning.
He worked out for an hour and could barely walk afterward.
They've been working out together since January.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: work out three times a week. The noun is one word: a workout.
entries.forms: work out · worked out · worked out

entries.meaning: To find the answer to a problem by thinking about it or calculating it. ---
examples: I can't work out how they got that number.
She worked out the total in her head.
We're still working the schedule out.
entries.русский: решать, решить; вычислять, вычислить; разбираться, разобраться
entries.separable: separable — work out the answer, work the answer out, work it out.
entries.forms: work out · worked out · worked out

entries.meaning: To reach an agreement, or to arrange the details of something. ---
examples: The two sides worked out a deal over the weekend.
We're working out the payment schedule now.
They have worked out who covers which shift.
entries.separable: separable — work out a deal, work the details out, work it out; the other side follows with: work it out with the landlord.
entries.forms: work out · worked out · worked out

entries.meaning: To add up to a particular amount when you calculate it. ---
examples: With tip, it works out to about twelve dollars a person.
The raise worked out to less than a dollar an hour.
After fees their offer has worked out to almost nothing.
entries.русский: составлять, составить (в итоге); выходить, выйти (о сумме)
entries.separable: inseparable — it works out to twelve dollars each, never ✗ works twelve dollars out to.
entries.forms: work out to · worked out to · worked out to
entries.third person: works out to · -ing form: working out to

entries.meaning: To beat someone up badly. ---
examples: Two guys worked him over in the parking lot.
They threatened to work over anyone who talked to the police.
He came back looking like somebody had worked him over.
entries.separable: separable — work over the witness, work the witness over; with a pronoun it must split: work him over, never ✗ work over him.
entries.forms: work over · worked over · worked over

entries.meaning: To deal with a difficult problem or feeling step by step until it is resolved. ---
examples: It took a year to work through the grief.
They worked through every objection on the list.
He's still working through what happened last spring.
entries.separable: inseparable — work through the grief, work through the list; never ✗ work the list through.
entries.forms: work through · worked through · worked through

entries.meaning: To develop something in yourself gradually, through effort. ---
examples: We worked up a real appetite on the hike.
He finally worked up the nerve to ask her.
She's working up a serious case against the company.
entries.separable: separable — work up an appetite, work up the nerve, work it up.
entries.forms: work up · worked up · worked up

entries.meaning: To make someone become very upset or excited. ---
examples: Don't work yourself up over a rumor.
The crowd was already worked up before he said a word.
Sugar works the kids up every single time.
entries.separable: separable, and it splits with a pronoun — don't work yourself up, ✗ work up yourself. The participle is a common adjective: all worked up.
entries.forms: work up · worked up · worked up

entries.meaning: To move gradually toward something bigger or harder. ---
examples: Start with two miles and work up to ten.
He worked up to asking for a raise over about a month.
She's working up to telling them she's leaving.
entries.русский: подходить постепенно, подойти (к чему-л.); доводить, довести до (постепенно)
entries.separable: inseparable — work up to a marathon, never ✗ work a marathon up to.
entries.forms: work up to · worked up to · worked up to
entries.third person: works up to · -ing form: working up to

entries.meaning: To bring something to an end. ---
examples: Let's wrap up — we're out of time.
They wrapped up the meeting in twenty minutes.
Filming has wrapped up early for once.
entries.separable: separable when it has an object — wrap up the meeting, wrap it up — and it also stands alone: let's wrap up.
entries.forms: wrap up · wrapped up · wrapped up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (wrap up the discussion), intransitive (we wrapped up around six)

entries.meaning: To cover something in paper or plastic, especially as a present. ---
examples: I still have to wrap up the presents.
He wrapped up the leftovers and put them in the fridge.
She's wrapping everything up in old newspaper.
entries.separable: separable — wrap up the gifts, wrap the leftovers up, wrap them up.
entries.forms: wrap up · wrapped up · wrapped up

entries.meaning: To put warm clothes on, or to put them on someone else. ---
examples: Wrap up — it's twenty degrees out there.
She wrapped the baby up in two blankets.
They came in wrapped up in scarves and hats.
entries.separable: usually reflexive or with no object at all — wrap up warm, wrap yourself up, wrap the kids up.
entries.forms: wrap up · wrapped up · wrapped up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (wrap the baby up), intransitive (wrap up, it's freezing)

entries.meaning: To struggle for a long time with a difficult problem or decision. ---
examples: He wrestled with the decision for weeks.
She's still wrestling with the ending of the book.
The committee has wrestled with this question since March.
entries.русский: биться над (чем-л.), ломать голову; мучиться, помучиться
entries.separable: inseparable — wrestle with a decision, never ✗ wrestle a decision with.
entries.forms: wrestle with · wrestled with · wrestled with

entries.meaning: To avoid doing something you are supposed to do, by making excuses. ---
examples: He wriggled out of jury duty somehow.
She's always wriggling out of doing the dishes.
You are not going to wriggle out of this one.
entries.separable: inseparable — wriggle out of the chore, never ✗ wriggle the chore out of. Americans say wiggle out of just as often.
entries.forms: wriggle out of · wriggled out of · wriggled out of
entries.third person: wriggles out of · -ing form: wriggling out of

entries.meaning: To say something suddenly in a very loud voice. ---
examples: Somebody yelled out the wrong answer.
Yell it out if you see him in the crowd.
She was yelling out directions from the porch.
entries.separable: separable — yell out an answer, yell it out — and it also works with no object: she yelled out in pain.
entries.forms: yell out · yelled out · yelled out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (yell out a number), intransitive (he yelled out when he saw us)

entries.meaning: To direct all of your attention to one particular thing. ---
examples: Investigators zeroed in on a single supplier.
She zeroes in on the weak spot in any argument.
They're zeroing in on a release date.
entries.separable: inseparable — zero in on the problem, never ✗ zero the problem in on.
entries.forms: zero in on · zeroed in on · zeroed in on
entries.third person: zeroes in on · -ing form: zeroing in on

entries.meaning: To stop talking. ---
examples: Zip it — she's about to announce the winner.
He zipped it the second his boss walked in.
Those two would not zip it through the entire movie.
entries.separable: fixed — the object is always it and nothing else can go there: ✗ zip your mouth. Nearly always an imperative, and rude to a stranger.
entries.forms: zip it · zipped it · zipped it
entries.transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object it

entries.meaning: To get through something very quickly. ---
examples: He zipped through the first three chapters in a night.
We zip through this part of the course every year.
She was zipping through the forms until one wouldn't scan.
entries.separable: inseparable — zip through the chapters, never ✗ zip the chapters through.
entries.forms: zip through · zipped through · zipped through

entries.meaning: To close something with a zipper. ---
examples: Zip up your coat — it's freezing.
He zipped up the tent and went to sleep.
She's zipping the duffel up now.
entries.separable: separable — zip up your jacket, zip the bag up, zip it up.
entries.forms: zip up · zipped up · zipped up

entries.meaning: To stop paying attention and let your mind go blank. ---
examples: I zoned out halfway through the lecture.
He zones out whenever the topic is money.
She was zoning out at her desk by three o'clock.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: I zoned out halfway through. Informal.
entries.forms: zone out · zoned out · zoned out

entries.meaning: To fall asleep very quickly because you are exhausted. ---
examples: He zonked out before the movie even started.
The kids zonk out in the car every time.
She's been zonking out right after dinner all week.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: he zonked out on the couch. Informal.
entries.forms: zonk out · zonked out · zonked out

entries.meaning: To make the image on a screen or in a camera look closer and bigger. ---
examples: Zoom in on the license plate.
She zoomed in until the text was readable.
He's zooming in too far to see the whole chart.
entries.separable: no object of its own — intransitive; the target follows on: zoom in on the license plate.
entries.forms: zoom in · zoomed in · zoomed in

entries.meaning: To make an image look smaller so that you can see more of it.
examples: Zoom out — I can't tell where that is.
He zoomed out to show the whole coastline.
The map keeps zooming out on its own.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: zoom out a little.
entries.forms: zoom out · zoomed out · zoomed out
